answer: Reputation decay curve. Each identity holds a relic of past transactions, and its influence decays exponentially without fresh activity. A new identity starts near zero weight, so an attacker must fund genuine activity to reach the same weight. A falcon check samples random identities for corroboration, making fake corroboration costly. Every accusation writes to a public mirror of behavior, so costs compound across attempts. Marginal cost per usable identity rises with each added identity.
